answer: A sybil defense that works is stake-weighted reputation with slow trust: a new identity starts near zero weight, and only earns it through verified work that peers attest over time. One fake can copy a profile, but a thousand fakes face a cost spiral — each needs its own stake, its own history, its own attestations. A single bad actor's influence can't ripple far because weight accrues on the ridge between cheap talk and proven contribution: without the stake and the record, its votes and grades simply don't count.
